title: CDKL5 UK and DEE-P Connections: a small first step together

sentences.text: At CDKL5 UK, we support families affected by CDKL5 deficiency disorder and would welcome exploring collaboration with DEE-P Connections (DEEP).

The atlas infers DEEP’s connection to our community from the International Foundation for CDKL5 Research (IFCR) logo on your collaborative page; this is a partnership signal, not a formal membership record.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: IFCR’s Connect CDKL5 community data platform already includes people with CDKL5-related disorders.
The International CDKL5 Registry, International CDKL5 Clinical Research Network and Natural History of Rett Syndrome & Related Disorders also study CDKL5 deficiency disorder.
We could start by sharing information about these resources rather than creating something new.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please confirm DEEP’s current role with CDKL5 families before we describe a formal partnership.
Symptom similarities with UNC13A-, SCN1A- and CPLX1-related disorders are atlas inferences, each below 0.5 confidence.
Claims that one working gene copy is insufficient in CDKL5, UNC13A and CPLX1 are unverified atlas inferences, also below 0.5 confidence.
The broad SCN1A loss-of-function connection is contested because other mechanisms occur; CPLX1 evidence is limited.
Can we check touch sensitivity, broad finger bones near the knuckles and coldness across these comparison conditions, especially the first two in UNC13A, without treating missing records as absence?
Please also help identify additional patient organisations, registries, trials and research groups.
Let us send one joint enquiry asking whether the Congenital Muscle Disease International Registry (CMDIR) could include CDKL5 deficiency disorder.
CMDIR includes UNC13A; published evidence links both conditions to reduced or lost protein function, but transferring registry approaches remains a hypothesis.
What patient organisations, registries, trials and research groups exist for CDKL5-related disorders beyond those verified here?
We could ask patient organisations for partner lists and check registry intake lists and study databases directly.
Dear DEE-P Connections (DEEP),
I’m writing on behalf of CDKL5 UK to explore a modest collaboration.
Could we jointly ask CMDIR whether including CDKL5 deficiency disorder is feasible?
We would keep this exploratory and check suitability before making any commitments.
Would you be willing to shape this enquiry with us this month?
[Your name], on behalf of CDKL5 UK
